title: Leaving the boat, joining the WPA band, and Pichon versus Robichaux battles of bands
summary: After leaving the boat he joined the WPA band; he also describes serious battles of bands between Pichon and Joe Robichaux at dances.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Were you in the WPA band?

No. Yes. That's what I was getting ready to come to. I thought it was something. Well, after we left the boat, then I got in the WPA band. Now, I wouldn't get it. That must have been in 41. In 41 or early part of 42. But I think it was in the late part of 41, around November, December. It might have been January of 42 or February. I know it was cold, see. Well, matter of fact, there wasn't I, nobody else in the WPA band. So, uh, well, I always was, I mean, I was still young. Of course, I got married then. See, I got married in 39, 1939, November, 39. And, uh, and I mean, I was always willing to keep my lip up. See, I even, even after we left the boat, see. So, uh, I don't know. There was some kind of controversy, I mean, that caused us to leave that boat, see, with the band and Pichon, you know. It seems as though, I mean, fast were very popular around New Orleans at that time, because dance bands were very popular. Because, uh, we used to play, uh, dances like at the, at the Santa Sinners Club. Okay. Okay. And that's the old Lions Club that I was talking about before. Yeah. Mm-hmm. And now it's called No Peace Undertaker. Well, we used to play, uh, uh, uh, dances there. And sometimes they would have Joe Robichaux's band, too. They would put on a battle of bands. Walter Fass Pichon and Joe Robichaux's band. And people took that so serious that it wasn't even funny. People would not dance. One band would play about four or five tunes, and everybody would gather in front of the band, and they'd applaud, you know. Mm-hmm. And then the other band would take over, and they'd honor, and they were very serious about that, you know. But what band's the best band? Well, matter of fact, the musicians were serious themselves. Yeah. Yeah, at that time, you know. Sure, that was something.
They give a prize or a cup or anything?

No, no, no prize on any cup or anything like that. But it's just a battle of bands, and, uh, I just can't explain it, man. I mean, see how serious people were, you know, at that time. They liked their music. Yeah. Yeah. See? Uh, now, something else I want to know. Oh, yeah, Bill. Uh, you know, I got a book inside. It's The Life of Louis Armstrong. Yeah. It's a pocket-sized magazine.
